In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether the magnetic field of the earth influences the behaviour of the honeybee.
the question of the influence of magnetic and photic conditions on the behaviour of dancing bees, and the question whether there is a correlation between the magnetic and photic reactions.
the question whether light and the EMF interact with each other in the dance behaviour.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the honey-bee's response to light depends on the magnetic conditions, and that the magnetic field can be used to influence the photic sensitivity of the honey-bee.
the magnetic field of the earth is an important stimulus for the dance of honey-bees.
the magnetic and photic responses are interdependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bees react to light only when they dance parallel or nearly parallel to the direction of the EMF, and that the time of total indifference varies with the magnetic field.
the bees are able to distinguish a magnetic field of the earth and a light stimulus.
the bees react to light only when they dance parallel with the inclination of the EMF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bees are sensitive to light under varying magnet conditions and this sensitivity is influenced by the inclination of the EMF.
the bees are able to detect and use the earth's magnetic inclination as a reference direction.
light and magnetic field influence the dancing behaviour of honeybees in a similar manner, i.e. by a maximum response at a specific inclination angle.
